mechanism_narrative: A lower federal funds rate directly reduces the risk-free rate, lowering the discount rate for equity valuation models and driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when FEDFUNDS is below 5.0%.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly CPI inflation rate above 3.5% (computed from CPIAUCSL) signals persistent inflation, prompting the Fed to maintain restrictive monetary policy and suppressing equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 55% of months when CPIAUCSL YoY inflation exceeds 3.5%.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) indicate a broad-based weakening in consumer demand, triggering a negative S&P 500 forward return over the next 60 trading days as recession risks rise.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when both HOUST and RSAFS decline for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: In a low unemployment regime (UNRATE < 3.5%), a further decline in unemployment signals tight labor market conditions that boost corporate profit margins and drive positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when UNRATE is below 3.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly industrial production index below 102.0 indicates a slowdown in manufacturing activity, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as recession fears intensify.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 55% of months when INDPRO falls below 102.0.

mechanism_narrative: A quarterly GDP growth rate above 2.0% (as measured by GDPC1) signals robust economic expansion, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days through increased corporate earnings.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of quarters when GDPC1 growth exceeds 2.0%.

mechanism_narrative: In a monetary tightening regime (FEDFUNDS > 5.0%), a further increase in the federal funds rate compresses equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when FEDFUNDS exceeds 5.0%.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly payroll growth rate below 0.1% (computed from PAYEMS) signals weakening labor market conditions, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as recession risks rise.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 55% of months when PAYEMS MoM growth falls below 0.1%.
